steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Power chords (root + fifth, no third) create a raw, powerful sound — they are ambiguous between major and minor, giving rock its aggressive character.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Drum kit in rock: kick drum (beats 1 and 3), snare (beats 2 and 4 = backbeat), hi-hat (subdivides the beat), crash cymbal (accents).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Studio production became a creative tool: automatic double-tracking (ADT) thickens vocal sound; reverb creates spatial depth; distortion adds harmonic richness.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Progressive rock expanded rock's structural scope: longer forms, classical influences, concept albums, complex time signatures and technical virtuosity.

steps.title: Try it yourself

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
